One main issue I faced with this course was homeworks. In this course, the homeworks need to be done through “mastering physics”. This website does not allow you to access the homeworks unless you turn off pop-up blockers. At the start of the year we were told to check the website regularly in case a new homework is assigned. I used to check regularly but at some point later in the semester, I was told by my friends that the THIRD HOMEWORK is assigned. Long story short, they told me that I need to turn off pop-up blockers which I was not informed about by the assistant and therefore, I missed two of my homeworks which not only means I lost credits but I also lost some valuable practice for my quizes and my course. So I emailed him and he said that I will not get any credits back because it is not his fault. I could have missed all of my homeworks if my friend did not text me because neither he website or the teacher would have informed me. Also I would say that the teacher should also tell if a homework is assigned or not so that if a student forgets or is facing problems could act before it is too late. So I would like to say that for the next students to come after me, the assistant should give full information regarding the course so they don’t lose any credits just like I did.

course:
This course is, without exaggeration, the single worst educational experience of my life as a student. It’s an unmitigated disaster, failing on every conceivable level. Lectures and homework have no connection to the exams, which are deliberately designed to confuse and demoralize rather than assess understanding. These exams aren’t a measure of knowledge; they’re an exercise in futility, filled with convoluted, impractical questions that no amount of preparation could solve.

After the first midterm shocked me with its absurd difficulty, I chose to dedicate an enormous amount of time to this course, hoping to salvage my grade. I sacrificed countless hours—time I should’ve devoted to far more relevant and helpful courses—to focus on this one. And yet, despite spending weeks studying relentlessly, the outcome stayed the same: my hard work meant nothing. This course doesn’t reward effort or mastery; it punishes both.

The grading system adds insult to injury. Despite scoring over 90 on every experiment, homework, quiz, and project, it was mathematically impossible to earn higher than a B or B+. Exams are weighted so heavily that everything else becomes irrelevant, making success unattainable no matter how prepared you are. It’s as if the course is designed to ensure failure or mediocrity, no matter how much effort you invest.

Physics was once a subject I loved, a field I was excited to explore and understand. This course has destroyed that entirely, replacing passion with frustration, resentment, and deep disappointment. It’s a masterclass in how to demotivate students and ruin their relationship with a subject.

I know this evaluation will likely fall on deaf ears, as this course has been a laughingstock among students for generations. However, this term hit an entirely new low—the absolute epitome of mismanagement and incompetence. One can only hope this is rock bottom because it’s hard to imagine how it could be worse.
